issue.title: on_change not able to access text_area text on initalization and later on uses old text_area value
issue.body:
### Checklist


### Summary

on_change not able to access text_area text on initalization and later on uses old text_area value as it could be seen in example below.
Note that old value issue could be resolved by replacing
st.session_state["text_area"] = st.text_area("example test", "hello form the textbox", on_change=update())
with
st.text_area("example test", "hello form the textbox", on_change=update(), key = "text_area"), but  it as I understood it unexpected behavior

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

def update():
    if "text_area" in st.session_state:
        st.write(st.session_state.text_area)
    else:
        st.write(st.session_state.temp_text)

st.session_state.temp_text = "no acess to text_area"
st.session_state["text_area"] = st.text_area("example test", "hello form the textbox", on_change=update())
```


### Steps To Reproduce

Run the script, see it states "no acess to text_area" above text area.
Type text in text_area pres crl+enter to apply changes

### Expected Behavior

show text_area text in each of the steps

### Current Behavior

as described in bug description

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version:1.26.0
- Python version: 3.11.4
- Operating System: win 11
- Browser: edge


### Additional Information

_No response_

Hi @vuksan314,

This is expected behavior. Callbacks are run before the main script run, so if you're setting `st.session_state["text_area"]` to the value from the `st.text_area` widget within the script run, the callback will have already run at that point, so a change to the text area won't be reflected. You'll need to set a `key` in the `st.text_area` widget for this to work as expected.
